gloss: cold snap; sharp drop in temperature; chill

definitions.gloss: cold snap; sharp drop in temperature; severe chill
definitions.explanation: A sudden or intense drop in temperature, typically referring to weather becoming noticeably cold.
A figurative cooling or worsening of a relationship, economy, or situation.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}の{冷|ひ}え{込|こ}みが{厳|きび}しい。
{今夜|こんや}は{冷|ひ}え{込|こ}みが{予想|よそう}されます。
examples.english: A cold snap is expected tonight.

examples.japanese: {放射冷却|ほうしゃれいきゃく}の{影響|えいきょう}で、{内陸部|ないりくぶ}は{厳|きび}しい{冷|ひ}え{込|こ}みとなるでしょう。
examples.english: Due to radiative cooling, inland areas will experience a severe cold snap.

examples.japanese: {景気|けいき}の{冷|ひ}え{込|こ}みが{続|つづ}いている。
{両国|りょうこく}の{関係|かんけい}に{冷|ひ}え{込|こ}みが{見|み}られる。
examples.english: A cooling is observed in the relations between the two countries.

examples.japanese: {消費|しょうひ}の{冷|ひ}え{込|こ}みにより、{小売業|こうりぎょう}の{売上|うりあげ}が{落|お}ちている。
examples.english: Due to the cooling of consumer spending, retail sales are declining.

notes:
The noun form of the compound verb {冷|ひ}え{込|こ}む (to get intensely cold). The {込|こ}む suffix adds a sense of thoroughness or depth — the cold penetrates deeply.

USAGE:
In weather contexts (sense 1), extremely common in forecasts and everyday conversation during autumn and winter. The figurative sense (sense 2) is standard in news and commentary about economic downturns or diplomatic cooling.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {冷|ひ}え{込|こ}みが{厳|きび}しい — the cold snap is severe
- {朝晩|あさばん}の{冷|ひ}え{込|こ}み — morning and evening chill
- {景気|けいき}の{冷|ひ}え{込|こ}み — economic downturn
- {消費|しょうひ}の{冷|ひ}え{込|こ}み — decline in consumer spending

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {寒|さむ}さ — coldness (general, simple)
- {冷|ひ}え — chill, coldness (simpler form, also used for body chills)
- {低迷|ていめい} — stagnation, slump (for economy/business, no temperature sense)
